To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the RAS plays an important role in the regulation of circadian blood pressure profiles in animal models of hypertension.
the RAS plays an important role in both the pathophysiology of hypertension and in circadian blood pressure regulation.
losartan reduced blood pressure dose-dependently in spontaneously hypertensive rat (SHR) but was more effective in TGR(mRen-2)27 rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the AII receptor antagonist losart-an on 24-h BP profiles of primary and secondary hypertensive rats.
the development of a new method for the determination of the circadian rhythm of the circadian BP profile.
a new animal model for the investigation of the pathomechanisms of hypertension and the development of new antihypertensive drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RAS plays a role in the regulation of circadian BP profiles in primary hypertension, whereas in secondary hypertension it is a major pathomechanistic factor.

AII receptor blockade and ACE inhibition in the rat models of primary and experimental secondary hypertension are effective in lowering blood pressure and normalizing circadian blood pressure profiles, and that the effects are more pronounced in the experimental secondary hypertension.
the circadian BP pattern is not a consequence of the hypertension itself but rather that the hypertension is a consequence of the circadian BP profile.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AII receptor antagonists and ACE inhibitors are more effective in lowering BP in secondary than in primary hypertension.
losartan is a more effective antihypertensive agent in TGR than in SHR, with greater and longer lasting BP reduction and a normalized circadian profile.
the renin-2 gene is the major cause for hypertension in TGR(mRen-2)27 and the renin- angiotensin system plays an important role in the pathophysiology of hypertension in these rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RAS plays an essential role in circadian blood pressure regulation.
the renin- angiotensin system plays a major role in circadian BP regulation.
losartan, a specific AII receptor antagonist, has a greater antihypertensive effect in TGR than in SHR, and that this effect is more pronounced when the drug is given at 0700 h.
